examples.ko: 요즘 입맛이 시원찮아서 밥을 반만 먹었어요.
examples.en: My appetite hasn't been great lately, so I only ate half my rice.
I got a disappointing report card, so I'm upset.

examples.ko: 그 식당은 음식 맛이 좀 시원찮아요.
examples.en: The food at that restaurant is a bit underwhelming.
The vacuum cleaner I just bought is really not up to much.
If the answer isn't satisfying, ask again.
You don't look so well today.

explain: '시원치 않다'의 준말이에요. 결과, 반응, 몸 상태가 기대만 못할 때 쓰고 '신통찮다'와 비슷해요. '시원찮은 대답', '입맛이 시원찮다'처럼 나쁜 평가를 말해요.
explain_en: It is the short form of '시원치 않다'. You use it when a result, a reaction or someone's condition falls short of what you hoped, much like '신통찮다'. It always gives a negative judgment, as in '시원찮은 대답' or '입맛이 시원찮다'.

examples.ko: 마트에서 새로 나온 주스를 시음해 봤어요.
examples.en: I sampled the new juice at the supermarket.

examples.ko: 오늘 카페에서 신메뉴 시음 행사를 해요.
examples.en: The cafe is holding a tasting event for new menu items today.

examples.ko: 사기 전에 먼저 시음할 수 있어요?
examples.en: Can I taste it before I buy?
Many people were sampling, so the line was long.
I tried the tea, and the aroma was really good.

examples.ko: 이 매장은 시음용 작은 컵도 줘요.
examples.en: This store also gives you small cups for tasting.

explain: 마시는 것에 써요. 먹어 보는 음식은 '시식하다'라고 해서 짝으로 알아 두면 좋아요. 마트나 카페에서 '시음 행사', '시음회'처럼 자주 보여요.
explain_en: It is used for drinks. For food you try, the matching word is '시식하다', so learn them as a pair. You often see it in '시음 행사' and '시음회' at supermarkets and cafes.

en: a married woman living with her in-laws

examples.ko: 요즘은 시집살이를 하는 며느리가 많지 않아요.
examples.en: These days not many daughters-in-law live with their in-laws.

examples.ko: 할머니는 젊을 때 시집살이가 정말 힘드셨대요.
examples.en: They say life with the in-laws was really hard for Grandma when she was young.
I was shocked by a scene about in-law life in the drama.
I heard she felt at ease after getting away from living with her in-laws.

examples.ko: 외할머니는 고된 시집살이를 십 년 동안 견디셨어요.
examples.en: My grandmother endured ten years of hard life with her in-laws.
It hurts to hear stories about life with the in-laws.

explain: 단순히 같이 사는 것보다 시부모 눈치를 보며 고생한다는 느낌이 강해요. '시집살이를 하다/시키다/겪다', '시집살이가 심하다'처럼 써요. 남편이 처가에서 사는 것은 '처가살이'라고 해요.
explain_en: It carries the feeling of hardship and walking on eggshells around the husband's parents, not just living together. It is used in '시집살이를 하다/시키다/겪다' and '시집살이가 심하다'. When a husband lives with his wife's family, it is called '처가살이'.

en: live with a married woman's in-laws

examples.ko: 저는 결혼하고 삼 년 동안 시집살이했어요.
examples.en: I lived with my in-laws for three years after getting married.

examples.ko: 시집살이하는 친구가 요즘 많이 지쳐 보여요.
examples.en: My friend who lives with her in-laws looks very tired lately.

examples.ko: 시부모님과 같이 살지만 시집살이한다고 느끼지 않아요.
examples.en: I live with my in-laws, but I don't feel like it's hard in-law life.
In the old days, a daughter-in-law had to live with her husband's family.
I heard she learned a lot of cooking while living with her in-laws.

examples.ko: 어머니는 시집살이하느라 친정에 자주 못 가셨어요.
examples.en: My mother couldn't visit her parents' home often because she was living with her in-laws.

explain: '시집살이를 하다'처럼 띄어서 써도 같은 뜻이에요. 주로 며느리의 입장에서 말하고, 힘들게 지냈다는 느낌이 함께 와요. 지금은 옛날 이야기나 드라마에서 더 자주 들려요.
explain_en: You can also split it as '시집살이를 하다' with the same meaning. It is told from the daughter-in-law's point of view and usually suggests a hard time. Today you hear it more in stories about the past and in dramas.

examples.en: There's a sour smell coming from the fridge.
This kimchi is over-fermented and tastes sour.
The milk has turned sour, so don't drink it.
I ate a lemon and now my mouth tastes sour.
I like the sour yet sweet taste of strawberries.
The sweat smelled sour.

explain: 맛뿐 아니라 냄새에도 많이 써요. '새콤하다'는 기분 좋은 신맛에 어울리고, '시큼하다'는 조금 더 강하거나 상한 느낌이 날 때도 써요. '시다'보다 부드럽게 신 느낌을 말할 때 좋아요.
explain_en: It describes smells as well as tastes. '새콤하다' suits a pleasant tartness, while '시큼하다' can feel stronger, or even like something has gone off. It is also a milder way to say something tastes sour than plain '시다'.

examples.en: We start a trial operation from this month.

examples.ko: 시험적으로 새 앱을 써 보고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm trying out the new app on a trial basis.
It's an experimental attempt, so we don't know the result yet.

examples.ko: 시험적 판매 기간에는 값이 더 싸요.
examples.en: During the trial sales period, the price is lower.

examples.ko: 우리 반은 시험적으로 수업 시간을 바꿨어요.
examples.en: Our class changed the lesson schedule on a trial basis.

examples.ko: 시험적 조치라서 문제가 있으면 다시 바꿀 거예요.
examples.en: It's a trial measure, so we'll change it again if there's a problem.

explain: '시험적 운영', '시험적 도입', '시험적 판매'처럼 뒤에 명사가 오거나 '시험적으로'의 꼴로 많이 써요. 대화에서는 '시험 삼아'가 더 쉬운 말이에요. 시험(test)이라는 말과 달리 학교 시험이 아니라 '해 보는 것'이라는 뜻으로 써요.
explain_en: It appears before nouns in '시험적 운영', '시험적 도입' and '시험적 판매', or as '시험적으로'. In conversation, '시험 삼아' is the easier way to say it. Despite the word 시험, it has nothing to do with school exams; it means trying something out.

examples.en: Thanks to the dishwasher, the time I spend on dishes has gone down.
I put the dishes in the dishwasher and pressed the button.
The new house comes with a dishwasher.

examples.ko: 이 냄비는 식기세척기로 씻으면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't wash this pot in the dishwasher.
The dishwasher is too noisy.
I compared prices because I want to buy a dishwasher.

explain: 말할 때는 줄여서 '식세기'라고 하는 사람이 많아요. '설거지'와 함께 외워 두면 좋고, '식기세척기를 돌리다'라고 자주 말해요.
explain_en: In speech many people shorten it to '식세기'. It pairs well with '설거지' (washing dishes), and people often say '식기세척기를 돌리다' for running it.

examples.en: I cook with plant-based oil.
Plant-based milk is made from soybeans or oats.
This cream is plant-based, so it's gentle on the skin.

examples.ko: 식물성 단백질을 더 먹으려고 두부를 사요.
examples.en: I buy tofu to eat more plant protein.
Plant and animal fats have different properties.
My younger sibling only eats plant-based food.

explain: '식물성 기름', '식물성 단백질'처럼 뒤에 명사를 붙여 써요. 반대말은 '동물성'이에요. 식품 포장이나 화장품 설명에서 자주 보여요.
explain_en: It is used before nouns, as in '식물성 기름' and '식물성 단백질'. The opposite is '동물성'. You often see it on food packages and cosmetics descriptions.

examples.en: Dust got in my eye, so I rinsed it with saline.
Keep your contact lenses in saline.
I bought a bottle of saline at the pharmacy.

examples.ko: 코가 막힐 때 식염수 스프레이를 써요.
examples.en: I use a saline spray when my nose is stuffy.
The nurse poured saline on the wound.
We've run out of saline, so I have to buy more.

explain: '소금물'은 집에서 소금을 탄 물에도 쓰지만, '식염수'는 눈, 코, 상처를 씻을 때 약국과 병원에서 쓰는 깨끗한 물이라는 느낌이에요. 렌즈 보관액이나 코 세척 이야기에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: '소금물' can mean any salty water, even one you mix at home, but '식염수' suggests clean medical-grade water used at pharmacies and hospitals for eyes, noses and wounds. It comes up often in talk about contact lenses and nasal rinses.

examples.ko: 식칼이 무뎌서 양파가 잘 안 썰려요.
examples.en: The kitchen knife is dull, so the onion won't cut well.
Mom cut the watermelon in half with a kitchen knife.

examples.ko: 식칼은 아이 손이 닿지 않는 곳에 두세요.
examples.en: Keep kitchen knives out of children's reach.
I bought a new kitchen knife and put it in the kitchen.
The handle of the kitchen knife has come loose, so it's dangerous.

examples.ko: 이 식칼은 고기도 생선도 잘 잘라요.
examples.en: This kitchen knife cuts both meat and fish well.

explain: 부엌에서 음식 재료를 자르는 칼이에요. 같은 뜻으로 '부엌칼'도 쓰고, 일상에서는 그냥 '칼'이라고 말하는 경우가 많아요. '식칼을 갈다'처럼 '갈다'와 자주 함께 써요.
explain_en: It is the knife used to cut ingredients in the kitchen. '부엌칼' means the same, and in daily talk people often just say '칼'. It often goes with the verb '갈다' (to sharpen), as in '식칼을 갈다'.

examples.en: The kitchen looks brighter after I laid a tablecloth.
The child spilled juice on the tablecloth.
I wash the tablecloth once a week.
Guests are coming, so I changed to a pretty tablecloth.
The tablecloth has a flower pattern, so it feels like spring.
The tablecloth is long, so it touches the floor.

explain: 식탁 전체에 까는 천이에요. 접시 아래에 놓는 작은 것은 '식탁 매트'라고 해서 달라요. '테이블보'라고도 많이 말하고, '식탁보를 깔다/걷다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It is the cloth that covers the whole table. The small one under a plate is a '식탁 매트', which is different. People also say '테이블보', and you use it as '식탁보를 깔다/걷다'.

examples.ko: 동생은 식탐이 많아서 늘 간식을 찾아요.
examples.en: My younger sibling is greedy about food and always looks for snacks.
It's really hard to resist the craving for food.

examples.ko: 식탐 때문에 저녁을 너무 많이 먹었어요.
examples.en: I ate too much dinner because of my greed for food.
Our puppy is incredibly greedy about food.

examples.ko: 식탐 많은 친구와 같이 먹으면 즐거워요.
examples.en: It's fun to eat with a friend who loves food so much.

examples.ko: 그는 식탐을 부리지 않고 천천히 먹어요.
examples.en: He eats slowly without being greedy.

explain: '식욕'은 먹고 싶은 마음 자체를 중립적으로 말하지만, '식탐'은 음식을 너무 욕심내는 느낌이 있어요. '식탐이 많다/있다', '식탐을 부리다'처럼 써요. '먹성'은 많이 잘 먹는 성질이라 조금 달라요.
explain_en: '식욕' neutrally means the wish to eat, but '식탐' suggests being too greedy for food. Use it as '식탐이 많다/있다' or '식탐을 부리다'. '먹성' is different: it is about how much and how well someone eats.

examples.en: We get our rice on a tray in the school cafeteria.
I stood in line holding my tray.
This tray has five compartments.
If you buy a tray for kids, washing up is easy.

examples.ko: 식판 위에 반찬을 골고루 담아 주세요.
examples.en: Please put a bit of each side dish on the tray.
Please return your finished tray over there.

explain: 칸이 나뉜 쟁반 모양 그릇이에요. 학교나 회사 구내식당, 어린이집에서 흔히 보여요. 집에서 아이에게 밥을 줄 때도 써서 '아기 식판'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is a tray-shaped dish with separate compartments, common in school and workplace cafeterias and daycare centers. At home it is also used for kids' meals, called '아기 식판'.

examples.en: My headaches keep coming back, so I booked an appointment at neurology.
The neurologist recommended a test.
You can get treatment for dizziness at neurology.
Which floor is neurology on in the hospital?
My father gets regular neurology checkups.
Neurology and psychiatry are different departments.

explain: '신경외과'는 수술을 하는 과라서 '신경과'와 달라요. 두통, 어지럼증, 손 떨림 같은 증상으로 갈 때 '신경과에 가다'라고 해요. 마음의 문제는 '정신건강의학과'에서 다뤄요.
explain_en: '신경외과' is the surgical department, so it differs from '신경과'. You go to '신경과' for symptoms like headaches, dizziness or trembling hands. Mental-health concerns are handled by '정신건강의학과'.

examples.en: He often shows irritable reactions.
Please don't slam the door in irritation.
My younger sibling answered in a snappy tone.
When I'm tired, I speak sharply without realizing it.

examples.ko: 신경질적인 사람과 일하면 눈치를 보게 돼요.
examples.en: Working with a touchy person makes you watch your step.
The cat made an irritated cry.

explain: '신경질을 내다'의 신경질에 '-적'이 붙은 말이에요. 단순히 예민한 것보다 짜증을 내며 날카롭게 반응하는 모습을 말해요. '예민하다'는 감각이나 반응이 민감하다는 뜻이라 조금 더 중립적이에요.
explain_en: It builds on 신경질 as in '신경질을 내다' (to get irritable). It describes reacting with irritation and sharpness, not merely being sensitive. '예민하다' is more neutral, meaning easily affected.

examples.ko: 그 회사는 신기술 개발에 많이 투자해요.
examples.en: That company invests a lot in developing new technology.
Thanks to new technology, the battery lasts long.
New technology has been applied to the new phone.
I take online lectures to learn new technology.
New technology is also widely used in agriculture.
Do you want to go to the new technology briefing together?

explain: '신기술 개발', '신기술 적용', '신기술 도입'처럼 뉴스나 회사 소개에서 자주 나와요. '최신 기술'은 지금 가장 새로운 기술이라는 느낌이 강하고, '신기술'은 새로 만들어진 기술 자체를 말해요.
explain_en: It shows up in news and company profiles in phrases like '신기술 개발', '신기술 적용' and '신기술 도입'. '최신 기술' stresses the very latest, while '신기술' refers to newly created technology itself.

examples.ko: 다음 주 금요일에 팀 신년회가 있어요.
examples.en: Our team has a New Year's party next Friday.
We talked about our plans for the new year at the party.
Where should we hold this year's New Year's party?

examples.ko: 저는 올해 신년회에 못 갈 것 같아요.
examples.en: I don't think I can make it to the New Year's party this year.
Alumni gathered and held a New Year's party.
We ate tteokguk together at the New Year's party.

explain: 연말 모임인 '송년회'와 짝이 되는 말이에요. 회사, 동호회, 동창회처럼 단체에서 새해에 처음 갖는 모임에 써요. 가족끼리 설날에 모이는 것은 보통 '신년회'라고 하지 않아요.
explain_en: It pairs with '송년회', the end-of-year gathering. It is used for the first get-together of a new year held by groups such as companies, clubs and alumni. A family gathering on Seollal is not usually called a '신년회'.

examples.en: Columbus is known for having discovered the New World.

examples.ko: 많은 사람이 신대륙으로 건너가 새 삶을 시작했어요.
examples.en: Many people crossed over to the New World and started new lives.
Crops from the New World were passed to Europe.

examples.ko: 역사 시간에 신대륙 탐험에 대해 배웠어요.
examples.en: In history class we learned about exploring the New World.
Potatoes and corn are crops that came from the New World.

examples.ko: 신대륙에 처음 도착한 배는 어떤 배였어요?
examples.en: What kind of ship was the first to reach the New World?

explain: 주로 아메리카 대륙을 유럽 사람의 관점에서 부르는 말이에요. 반대로 유럽, 아시아, 아프리카는 '구대륙'이라고 해요. 역사 수업이나 책에서 주로 보이고 일상 대화에서는 잘 안 써요.
explain_en: It mainly refers to the Americas as seen from a European point of view. The opposite is '구대륙' for Europe, Asia and Africa. You mostly meet it in history classes and books, not in everyday talk.

examples.en: My mother is looking for a good husband candidate.
He is popular as a marriage candidate.

examples.ko: 신랑감 소개 좀 해 달라고 부탁했어요.
examples.en: I asked someone to introduce me to a potential husband.
What kind of person would you like your future husband to be?
In the old days, parents picked the groom for you.
Aren't the requirements for a husband too picky?

explain: 결혼식장에 선 '신랑'과 달라서, 앞으로 결혼 상대가 될 만한 남자를 말해요. 여자 쪽은 '신붓감'이라고 해요. '신랑감으로 좋다'처럼 상대를 평가하는 말이라 조심해서 쓰세요.
explain_en: Unlike '신랑' (the groom at the wedding), this means a man who could become a marriage partner. The counterpart for women is '신붓감'. It evaluates a person, as in '신랑감으로 좋다', so use it with care.

examples.ko: 이 조사 결과는 신뢰성이 높지 않아요.
examples.en: The reliability of this survey result is not high.
Please find reliable materials.
I'm worried about whether the reviews can be trusted.
To boost credibility, you need to state your sources.
You need a habit of checking how reliable the news is.
This product passed a reliability test.

explain: '신뢰'는 사람이나 조직에 대한 믿음에도 쓰지만, '신뢰성'은 정보, 자료, 제품이 믿을 만한 정도를 말할 때 잘 어울려요. '신뢰성이 높다/낮다/있다/없다'처럼 써요. 대화에서는 '믿을 만하다'가 더 쉬워요.
explain_en: '신뢰' can be trust in people or organizations, but '신뢰성' fits how trustworthy information, data or products are. Use it as '신뢰성이 높다/낮다/있다/없다'. In casual talk, '믿을 만하다' is easier.

examples.en: My aunt is looking for a kind bride candidate.
She was very popular as a marriage candidate.
My older brother laughs whenever the topic of a bride comes up.
My mother said she would introduce me to a potential bride.
I asked whether he liked the woman as a potential bride.
What kind of person would you like your future wife to be?

explain: 앞으로 신부가 될 만한 여자를 말하고, 남자 쪽은 '신랑감'이에요. '신부'와 '감' 사이에 사이시옷이 들어가 '신붓감'이라고 써요. 상대를 평가하는 말이라 조심해서 쓰세요.
explain_en: It means a woman who could become a bride, with '신랑감' as the male counterpart. An 시옷 is added between 신부 and 감, giving '신붓감'. It evaluates a person, so use it with care.

examples.ko: 백화점 오 층에 남성 정장을 파는 신사복 매장이 있어요.
examples.en: There's a men's wear shop selling suits on the fifth floor of the department store.

examples.ko: 면접 때 입으려고 신사복을 한 벌 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought a suit to wear to my interview.
My father goes to work in a suit and tie.
I went to the shop to get measured for a suit.
This suit is a bit big in the shoulders.
Is it okay to wear a suit to the wedding?

explain: 주로 남자 정장을 파는 가게나 코너 이름으로 보여요. 말할 때는 '양복'이나 '정장'을 더 자연스럽게 쓰는 경우가 많아요. '정장'은 여자 옷에도 쓰지만 '신사복'은 남자 옷이에요.
explain_en: You mostly see it as the name of a shop or section selling men's suits. In speech, '양복' or '정장' often sounds more natural. '정장' can refer to women's formal wear too, but '신사복' is men's clothing.

examples.ko: 그는 늘 신사적 태도로 사람을 대해요.
examples.en: He always treats people in a gentlemanly manner.
Your message gets across even if you speak politely.
After the game they shook hands in a sportsmanlike way.
His gentlemanly behavior left a good impression.
Even when I'm angry, I want to settle things civilly.
I was surprised by his gentlemanly manners.

explain: 신사처럼 예의 바르고 점잖다는 뜻이라 칭찬으로 써요. 사람의 태도뿐 아니라 경기나 다툼을 '신사적으로' 끝낸다고도 말해요. 성별과 상관없이 점잖은 태도에도 쓸 수 있어요.
explain_en: It praises someone for being polite and well-mannered like a gentleman. It describes not only a person's attitude but also how a game or dispute is handled, as in '신사적으로'. It can also be used for polite conduct regardless of gender.

examples.ko: 신석기 시대 사람들은 농사를 짓기 시작했어요.
examples.en: People in the Neolithic era began to farm.
I saw Neolithic pottery at the museum.
I studied the difference between the Neolithic and Bronze Ages.
Neolithic ruins were found in our neighborhood.
In the Neolithic, people lived together in one place.

examples.ko: 이 그릇은 신석기 때 만든 거래요.
examples.en: They say this bowl was made in the Neolithic.

explain: 보통 '신석기 시대'처럼 말해요. 앞선 '구석기'와 뒤따르는 '청동기'를 함께 알아 두면 역사 이야기를 이해하기 쉬워요. 역사 수업, 박물관, 책에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is usually said as '신석기 시대'. Learn it together with the earlier '구석기' and the later '청동기' to follow history talk easily. It comes up in history classes, museums and books.

examples.ko: 제 친구는 반도체 연구소에서 신소재를 연구해요.
examples.en: My friend researches new materials at a semiconductor lab.
This bag is made of a lightweight new material.

examples.ko: 신소재 덕분에 옷이 더 얇고 따뜻해졌어요.
examples.en: Thanks to a new material, the clothes became thinner and warmer.
I saw news that they succeeded in developing a new material.
New materials are also used in cars.
I want to major in materials engineering at university.

explain: 새로 개발된 소재를 말하고, 뉴스나 광고에서 자주 나와요. '소재'는 만드는 데 쓰는 재료라서 '재료'와 비슷하지만, '신소재'는 특별히 새 기술로 만든 것이라는 느낌이 있어요. 대학 학과 이름에도 많이 쓰여요.
explain_en: It refers to a newly developed material and is common in news and advertising. '소재' is close to '재료', but '신소재' suggests something made with new technology. It is also widely used in university department names.

examples.en: We remodeled Grandma's kitchen in a modern style.
It's a modern building, so it even has an elevator.

examples.ko: 이 학교는 신식 시설을 갖추고 있어요.
examples.en: This school has modern facilities.
Using the newer machine made the work faster.
The new style is more convenient than the old way.

examples.ko: 그 가게는 낡았지만 주방은 신식이라 깨끗해요.
examples.en: The shop is old, but the kitchen is up to date, so it's clean.

explain: 반대말은 '구식'이에요. 옛날 방식과 비교해서 새롭다는 느낌이라, 지금은 '최신식'이나 '현대식'이 더 자주 들려요. '신식 건물', '신식 시설'처럼 뒤에 명사를 붙여 써요.
explain_en: The opposite is '구식'. It feels new in comparison to old ways, so '최신식' or '현대식' are also heard often today. Use it before nouns, as in '신식 건물' and '신식 시설'.

examples.en: A new fried chicken shop opened in our neighborhood.
They give free drinks to celebrate the grand opening.

examples.ko: 가게 앞에 신장개업이라고 쓴 현수막이 걸려 있어요.
examples.en: A banner saying grand opening hangs in front of the shop.
It was the first day of opening, so there were a lot of customers.
I received a grand opening discount coupon.
I heard my uncle will soon open a new shop.

explain: 가게를 새로 열거나 새롭게 단장해 다시 열 때 간판과 현수막에 많이 쓰는 말이에요. 일상 대화에서는 '새로 열다', '오픈하다'라고 더 자주 말해요. 'XX 신장개업'처럼 가게 홍보에서 눈에 띄어요.
explain_en: It is a phrase often seen on signs and banners when a shop opens anew or reopens after a refresh. In everyday talk people more often say '새로 열다' or '오픈하다'. You will notice it in shop promotions like 'XX 신장개업'.

examples.en: The applicant, please sign this document.
There are many applicants, so processing is slow.
Please write down the applicant's name and contact number.
We notify the applicant of the result by text message.
The applicant has to visit in person.
There are twenty scholarship applicants in total.

explain: 서류, 관공서, 법원에서 쓰는 격식 있는 말이에요. 일상에서는 '신청자'가 더 자연스럽고, 상대방을 '신청인'이라고 부르는 일은 거의 없어요. 서류에서는 '신청인'과 '대리인'을 구분해서 적어요.
explain_en: It is a formal word used on documents and at government offices and courts. '신청자' sounds more natural in daily life, and you rarely address someone directly as '신청인'. On forms, '신청인' is written separately from '대리인' (agent).

examples.ko: 신체장애가 있어도 일할 수 있는 직장이 늘고 있어요.
examples.en: Workplaces where people with physical disabilities can work are increasing.

examples.ko: 이 건물에는 신체장애 학생을 위한 엘리베이터가 있어요.
examples.en: This building has an elevator for students with physical disabilities.

examples.ko: 사고로 신체장애를 얻은 분이 강연을 하셨어요.
examples.en: A person who acquired a physical disability in an accident gave a talk.
Support differs depending on the degree of disability.

examples.ko: 신체장애 때문에 불편한 점을 이야기해 주셨어요.
examples.en: They told us about the inconveniences caused by their physical disability.

examples.ko: 신체장애 여부는 서류에 적지 않아도 돼요.
examples.en: You don't have to write whether you have a physical disability on the form.

explain: 서류와 제도, 뉴스에서 쓰는 격식 있는 말이에요. 일상에서는 그냥 '장애'라고 하고, 사람을 가리킬 때는 '장애인'이라고 해요. 눈이 불편한 것은 '시각장애', 팔다리는 '지체장애'처럼 나눠서 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: It is a formal term used in paperwork, systems and news. In daily life people simply say '장애', and for a person '장애인'. It can be narrowed down as '시각장애' (visual) or '지체장애' (limbs).

examples.en: This watch is brand new and unused.
New items are much more expensive than used ones.
Check the price of a new one first.
I bought a used item online that looks brand new.

examples.ko: 상자도 안 뜯은 신품을 반값에 팔아요.
examples.en: I'm selling a brand new, unopened item for half price.
If it breaks, we'll replace it with a new one.

explain: 반대말은 '중고품'이에요. 중고 거래 글이나 제품 설명에서 자주 보이고, 일상 대화에서는 '새 거', '새 제품'이라고 해요. '신품급'은 새것과 거의 같은 상태라는 뜻으로 중고 거래에서 써요.
explain_en: The opposite is '중고품'. You often see it in secondhand listings and product descriptions, while in conversation people say '새 거' or '새 제품'. '신품급' is used in secondhand trading for items in nearly new condition.

examples.en: I changed the room lighting to a warm color.
If the indoor lighting is dim, my eyes get tired.
I like this cafe because the lighting is soft.
The photo came out yellow because of the indoor lighting.

examples.ko: 공부방 실내조명은 너무 밝지 않게 하세요.
examples.en: Don't make the lighting in the study room too bright.
I picked out the room lighting myself in the new house.

explain: 집이나 가게 안의 불빛을 말하고, 인테리어 이야기에서 자주 나와요. 그냥 '조명'이라고 해도 대부분 통해요. '실내조명이 밝다/어둡다/은은하다'처럼 분위기를 표현할 때도 써요.
explain_en: It refers to the lighting inside a home or shop and comes up in interior design talk. Just saying '조명' usually works too. It is also used to describe atmosphere, as in '실내조명이 밝다/어둡다/은은하다'.

examples.en: The child sings while tapping the xylophone.
I played the xylophone for the first time in music class.
The xylophone sounds clear and is pleasant to hear.
A xylophone is an instrument you hit with mallets.
They have xylophone lessons at kindergarten.
I played a simple children's song on the xylophone.

explain: '실로폰을 치다'처럼 '치다'를 쓰고, 막대로 두드리는 악기라 '두드리다'도 어울려요. 초등학교 음악 시간에 자주 쓰는 악기예요. 영어 xylophone의 소리를 옮긴 외래어예요.
explain_en: Say '실로폰을 치다' with the verb '치다'; because you strike it with sticks, '두드리다' also fits. It is a common instrument in elementary music class. It is a loanword from the English 'xylophone'.

examples.ko: 도로 가운데 실선을 넘으면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not cross the solid line in the middle of the road.

examples.ko: 종이에 실선과 점선을 각각 그어 보세요.
examples.en: Draw a solid line and a dotted line on the paper.
Please cut along the solid line with scissors.
On the map, solid lines show roads.
In the graph, the solid line is this year's sales.
Please draw it with a solid line, not a dotted one.

explain: 반대말은 '점선'이에요. 그래프, 도면, 도로 차선 이야기에서 두 선을 구분할 때 함께 나와요. '실선을 긋다/그리다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: The opposite is '점선' (dotted line). The two appear together when distinguishing lines in graphs, drawings and road markings. Use it as '실선을 긋다/그리다'.

examples.ko: 실습비는 학기 초에 한 번 내요.
examples.en: We pay the lab fee once at the start of the semester.
This course has a separate practical training fee.

examples.ko: 실습비로 재료를 사서 요리 수업을 해요.
examples.en: We buy ingredients with the practice fee and hold the cooking class.

examples.ko: 실습비를 내지 않으면 수업에 참여할 수 없어요.
examples.en: If you don't pay the practice fee, you can't take part in the class.
Be sure to keep the receipt for the practice fee.
The school covers part of the practice fee.

explain: 등록금과 달리 수업에서 실제로 해 보는 활동에 드는 비용이에요. 요리, 미용, 간호, 실험 수업처럼 재료나 장비가 필요한 과목에서 자주 나와요. '실습비를 내다/걷다'와 함께 써요.
explain_en: Unlike tuition, it covers the cost of hands-on class activities. It comes up in subjects needing materials or equipment, such as cooking, beauty, nursing and lab classes. It goes with '실습비를 내다/걷다'.

examples.ko: 저는 이번 여름에 병원에서 실습생으로 일해요.
examples.en: This summer I'm working as a trainee at a hospital.
It's my first time as a trainee, so everything feels unfamiliar.
I explained the tasks to the trainee step by step.
Three trainees joined the company.
I walk around with a trainee name tag around my neck.

examples.ko: 실습생은 한 달 동안 현장을 배워요.
examples.en: Trainees learn about the workplace for one month.

explain: 학교 과정의 하나로 현장에서 배우러 온 학생이라는 느낌이 강해요. 회사에서 일하는 '인턴'과 비슷하지만, '실습생'은 학교 수업과 연결된 경우가 많아요. 병원, 학교, 공장에서 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
explain_en: It strongly suggests a student who comes to learn on site as part of a school program. It is close to '인턴', but '실습생' is more often tied to schoolwork. It is common at hospitals, schools and factories.

examples.ko: 소매 끝에 실오라기가 길게 늘어져 있어요.
examples.en: A long loose thread is hanging from the cuff.
Please pick the loose thread off my pants.
Hair as thin as a thread was blowing around.
The finish is neat, so I can't even see a loose thread.
I tidied up without leaving even a single thread.

examples.ko: 이 스웨터는 세탁하면 실오라기가 많이 나와요.
examples.en: This sweater sheds a lot of threads when washed.

explain: 옷에서 풀리거나 떨어져 나온 아주 가는 실 한 가닥을 말해요. '실밥'은 바느질한 자리에 보이는 실이라서 조금 달라요. 아주 작은 양을 강조할 때 '실오라기 하나'라고도 써요.
explain_en: It means a single very thin strand of thread that has come loose from clothing. '실밥' is the thread seen along a stitched seam, so it differs slightly. People also say '실오라기 하나' to stress how tiny an amount is.

examples.ko: 초콜릿은 실온에 두면 녹을 수 있어요.
examples.en: Chocolate can melt if left at room temperature.
Most metals are solid at room temperature.
This bread can be stored at room temperature.

examples.ko: 냉장고에서 꺼낸 우유가 실온으로 돌아올 때까지 기다려요.
examples.en: I wait until the milk from the fridge returns to room temperature.

examples.ko: 이 소스는 개봉 후에는 실온 보관이 안 돼요.
examples.en: This sauce can't be stored at room temperature once opened.

examples.ko: 실온 상태의 물을 마시는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: It's good to drink water at room temperature.

explain: 음식이나 약의 보관 방법을 말할 때 '냉장', '냉동'과 나란히 자주 나와요. '상온'도 비슷하게 쓰지만, 포장지에는 '실온 보관'이라고 쓰는 경우가 많아요. 방 안 공기의 온도를 말하는 '실내 온도'와도 가까운 말이에요.
explain_en: It often sits beside '냉장' (refrigerated) and '냉동' (frozen) when talking about storing food or medicine. '상온' is used similarly, but packages often say '실온 보관'. It is also close to '실내 온도' (indoor temperature).

examples.en: A loud noise is coming from the air conditioner's outdoor unit.
The outdoor unit is installed outside the balcony.
In summer, the area around the outdoor unit gets very hot.

examples.ko: 실외기 위에 물건을 올려 두지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't put things on top of the outdoor unit.

examples.ko: 실외기가 고장 나서 시원한 바람이 안 나와요.
examples.en: The outdoor unit is broken, so no cool air comes out.
When I moved, I took the outdoor unit to the new house.

explain: 방 안에 있는 '실내기'와 짝을 이루는 말이에요. 에어컨 이야기에서 가장 많이 나와요. 소리가 나거나 고장 나면 '실외기 때문에 그래요'처럼 원인을 말할 때도 써요.
explain_en: It pairs with '실내기', the indoor unit. It comes up mostly in talk about air conditioners. When there is noise or a breakdown, people name it as the cause, as in '실외기 때문에 그래요'.

examples.ko: 실지로 가 보니 사진보다 훨씬 좋았어요.
examples.en: When I actually went there, it was much better than in the photos.

examples.ko: 말은 쉽지만 실지로 해 보면 어려워요.
examples.en: It's easy to say, but hard when you actually try.
I heard they made a movie out of something that really happened.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 실지로 만나면 훨씬 친절해요.
examples.en: He is much kinder in person.

examples.ko: 실지로 먹어 보니까 생각보다 맵지 않아요.
examples.en: Having actually tried it, it isn't as spicy as I thought.
Let's check whether the rumor was actually true.

explain: '실제로'와 뜻이 비슷해서 바꿔 써도 돼요. 생각이나 말과 달리 직접 해 보았을 때를 말할 때 어울려요.
explain_en: It is close in meaning to '실제로' and the two can be swapped. It fits when you contrast ideas or words with what you find when you actually try something yourself.

examples.en: A training program for people who lost their jobs is opening.
I went to apply for the support fund for the unemployed.
The factory closed, so the number of jobless people grew.
My uncle was out of work for a while.

examples.ko: 실직자는 구직 상담을 무료로 받을 수 있어요.
examples.en: Jobless people can get job-search counseling for free.
The news said the number of people who lost their jobs has dropped.

explain: 일하던 곳에서 일자리를 잃은 사람을 가리켜요. '실업자'는 일이 없는 사람 전체를 넓게 말하지만, '실직자'는 직장을 잃었다는 점이 더 강해요. 직접 사람에게 쓰면 기분이 상할 수 있어서 뉴스나 지원 제도에서 주로 써요.
explain_en: It refers to someone who has lost the job they had. '실업자' broadly means anyone without work, while '실직자' stresses losing a job. Saying it directly to a person can hurt feelings, so it is mainly used in news and support programs.

examples.en: He is a doer who acts before he talks.

examples.ko: 환경 실천가로 알려진 분이 강연하러 왔어요.
examples.en: A person known as an environmental activist came to give a talk.
We need people who act more than we need good plans.

examples.ko: 우리 팀에는 실천가 같은 사람이 있어요.
examples.en: There's someone on our team who is a real doer.
A doer turns thoughts into action right away.

examples.ko: 저도 작은 일부터 하는 실천가가 되고 싶어요.
examples.en: I also want to be a doer who starts with small things.

explain: 생각이나 말에 그치지 않고 행동으로 옮기는 사람에게 쓰는 칭찬이에요. '이론가'와 짝이 되는 말로, 아는 것만 많은 사람과 비교해서 쓰기도 해요. '환경 실천가'처럼 앞에 분야를 붙여 쓰기도 해요.
explain_en: It is a compliment for someone who acts instead of only thinking or talking. It pairs with '이론가' (theorist), and is sometimes used to contrast with people who only know a lot. You can put a field in front, as in '환경 실천가'.

examples.ko: 저는 한 번 실패했다고 실패자는 아니에요.
examples.en: Failing once doesn't make me a failure.
You shouldn't call him a failure.
I think of them as challengers, not failures.
Even someone who has failed can get back up.
There is a lot to learn from the stories of those who failed.

examples.ko: 그 책은 실패자들의 경험을 모은 책이에요.
examples.en: That book collects the experiences of people who failed.

explain: 사람에게 '실패자'라고 하면 평가가 아주 강해서 상대를 낮추는 말이 될 수 있어요. 그래서 보통 '실패한 사람'이라고 풀어 말하거나, 위의 예문처럼 '아니다'와 함께 써요. 결과물에는 '실패작'을 써요.
explain_en: Calling a person a '실패자' is a harsh judgment and can be belittling. So people usually say '실패한 사람' instead, or use it with a negative as in the examples. For an outcome or product, use '실패작'.

examples.en: They say that movie was a box-office flop.
My first cake was a complete failure.
This dish was a flop, so I have to throw it away.
Even a failed work is a valuable experience.
That game was rated as a failure.

examples.ko: 제 첫 그림은 실패작이지만 버리지 않았어요.
examples.en: My first painting was a failure, but I didn't throw it away.

explain: 만든 결과물에 쓰는 말로, 요리, 영화, 그림, 제품 모두 가능해요. 반대말은 '성공작'이고, 아주 훌륭한 작품은 '걸작'이라고 해요. 사람에게는 쓰지 않고 '실패자'를 따로 써요.
explain_en: It is used for things people made, such as dishes, films, paintings and products. The opposite is '성공작', and an outstanding work is a '걸작'. It is not used for people; '실패자' is a separate word.
